The first thing that got me thinking about this issue was the way that we treat alcohol and drugs in this country. Now, regardless of how you feel about alcohol and drugs, we can surely agree that there is a parental nature to the authorities prohibiting you from doing what you want with your body, under threat of being locked in a cage. And that's the key - again, it doesn't matter if you think drugs being illegal and the drinking age being higher than the recruitment age are good things or not. All that matters is that there is a parental nature to this, where you are not free to make your own decision. Legally, you are an adult at age 18, and yet you are not legally permitted to make your own decisions in these areas (in the case of drugs, ever).

My next clue as to what was going on was when I noticed something - as I got older, the people around me started to talk about themselves when they were young as though they had no idea what was going on. I don't know about you guys, but when I was a teenager, sure I was more fearless, wreckless and didn't know as much - but I wasn't an idiot. In fact, I thought I was able to see the foils of adults who became battered down by the world and sought to live safe and easy lives. The aforementioned perspective of teenagers not being equipped to deal with the world around them has been used to justify everything from cerfew laws to trying to socially neuter them.

Finally, where it all really clicked for me in the realization that this is an INTENTIONAL effort to keep people in a state of arrested development is when the credit bill passed sometime back in 2008 (or so) that made the youngest age at which someone can apply for a credit card as 21. If this trend continues, 21 will become the new age at which someone is deemed an adult. At which point, people will start talking about how poor choices 21 year-olds make and that 25 should be the new age of adulthood.

Long story short, people accept the responsibility given to them (usually). Some teenagers are capable of being parents and some 50-year olds can't stay sober long enough to apply for a job. Socially created arrested development only undermines the gusto and lack of cynicism of youth and thus, empowers the old and jaded in a democratic society. Power is a zero-sum game - if you can take it away from someone else, yours is worth more.
